observations.assertion: A wider rectangular central entrance opening is framed by broad stone piers. Within it, glazed double door leaves sit between narrow fixed glazed side strips; a separate rectangular glazed/dark transom sits above the leaves. Adjacent ordinary tall window bays lie outside the entrance piers. Door-bottom/pavement detail is partly hidden by bicycles and scooters.

The doorway transom is below a level stone header/cornice. A separate clerestory glazed band is above that header, bounded by a horizontal pale upper frame, with the dark exhibit-box wall farther above. The doorway transom and high clerestory must remain separate assemblies.

The central header and upper frame are visible and horizontal. There is no triangular stone pediment across the central clerestory at the position authored by the street-side triangle. Thin branches do not conceal a solid triangle of that scope. White triangular shapes inside glazing read as interior/reflection pixels, not a stone facade pediment. Other rooflines and historical states are not exhaustively established.

White DE PLANTAGE is present within the doorway transom below the cornice. This establishes the real sign location only; exact dimensions, current state and defining architectural status remain unresolved. Do not reinstate the removed lettering during the geometry repair.
Wide street view supports low hall between taller end pavilions and the street-side alignment. Obliquity and trees limit central doorway subdivision evidence.
